views.name: addresses_with_both_line1_and_line2
views.body_sql: SELECT address_id, line_1, line_2, line_3, city, zip_postcode, state_province_county, country, other_address_details FROM Addresses WHERE line_1 IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(line_1) <> '' AND line_2 IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(line_2) <> ''
views.description: All address records that have both non-null, non-empty address line_1 and address line_2 (keeps address_id and the address lines and other address fields for reuse).

provenance.question: what are all the addresses including line 1 and line 2?
provenance.rewrite:
Task: Return all addresses with both address line 1 and address line 2 included for each address record
Required outputs: address line 1; address line 2
Filters: include all rows where address line 1 is not NULL or empty and address line 2 is not NULL or empty (i.e., both lines present)

tests.purpose: View grain/uniqueness: no duplicate address_id in the view
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT address_id FROM addresses_with_both_line1_and_line2 GROUP BY address_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 1) AS t

tests.purpose: Intrinsic filter: every row in the view has non-null, non-empty (trimmed) line_1 and line_2
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM addresses_with_both_line1_and_line2 v WHERE v.line_1 IS NULL OR TRIM(v.line_1) = '' OR v.line_2 IS NULL OR TRIM(v.line_2) = ''

tests.purpose: Reconciliation with base table: every view row exists in Addresses and has identical address fields
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM addresses_with_both_line1_and_line2 v LEFT JOIN Addresses a USING(address_id) WHERE a.address_id IS NULL OR ( (v.line_1 IS NOT a.line_1) OR (v.line_2 IS NOT a.line_2) OR (v.line_3 IS NOT a.line_3) OR (v.city IS NOT a.city) OR (v.zip_postcode IS NOT a.zip_postcode) OR (v.state_province_county IS NOT a.state_province_county) OR (v.country IS NOT a.country) OR (v.other_address_details IS NOT a.other_address_details) )

views.name: department_degree_counts
views.body_sql: SELECT d.department_id, d.department_name, COUNT(dp.degree_program_id) AS degree_count FROM Departments d LEFT JOIN Degree_Programs dp ON d.department_id = dp.department_id GROUP BY d.department_id, d.department_name
views.description: Per-department counts of degree programs (department id, department name, and number of degrees) to support queries comparing or ranking departments by how many degrees they offer.
validated_on: What is the name and id of the department with the most number of degrees ?
How many departments offer any degree?
How many different departments offer degrees?

provenance.question: Which department offers the most number of degrees? List department name and id.
provenance.rewrite:
Task: Find the department (name and id) that offers the largest number of degrees and return that department's name and id.
Required outputs: department name; department id
Filters: Consider all departments and all degree records; count degrees per department and select the department(s) with the maximum count.

tests.purpose: No duplicate rows at the declared grain (department_id, department_name).
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT department_id, department_name, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM department_degree_counts GROUP BY department_id, department_name HAVING cnt > 1)

tests.purpose: degree_count matches count of Degree_Programs per department (including zero) as computed from base tables.
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM department_degree_counts v LEFT JOIN Departments d ON v.department_id = d.department_id WHERE (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Degree_Programs dp WHERE dp.department_id = v.department_id) IS NOT v.degree_count

tests.purpose: Keys are not NULL: department_id and department_name must be present for every row.
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM department_degree_counts WHERE department_id IS NULL OR department_name IS NULL

positive_subgoals:
Task: Find the department that has the largest number of degrees and return that department's name and id.
Required outputs: department name; department id
Filters: Consider all departments in the departments table (no additional filters).; Count the number of degree records associated with each department using the degrees table's department reference.; If multiple departments tie for the maximum number of degrees, return all departments that share that maximum count.
Sort/limit: order by department id ascending (optional); no row limit unless used to break ties

Task: Compute the number of distinct departments that offer any degree (i.e., count departments for which there exists at least one degree they offer).
Required outputs: count_of_departments_offering_any_degree
Filters: include a department only if there exists at least one associated degree record indicating that the department offers that degree (i.e., exclude departments with zero associated degree records)

Task: Count the number of distinct departments that offer degrees.
Required outputs: a single integer value equal to the count of distinct department identifiers or names that offer at least one degree
Filters: only include departments that have at least one associated degree (i.e., departments linked to one or more degree records)

views.name: course_section_counts
views.body_sql: SELECT c.course_id, c.course_name, COUNT(s.section_id) AS section_count FROM Courses c LEFT JOIN Sections s ON c.course_id = s.course_id GROUP BY c.course_id, c.course_name
views.description: Per-course counts of sections (one row per course with its id, name, and number of associated sections).
counter_examples: What are the names and ids of every course with less than 2 sections?

provenance.question: What are the names and id of courses having at most 2 sections?
provenance.rewrite:
Task: Return the course names and course ids for courses that have at most 2 sections in the database.
Required outputs: course name; course id
Filters: count of sections associated with the course <= 2

tests.purpose: No duplicate rows for the declared grain (course_id, course_name).
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM course_section_counts v JOIN (SELECT course_id, course_name, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM course_section_counts GROUP BY course_id, course_name HAVING cnt>1) d USING(course_id, course_name)

tests.purpose: section_count matches count of Sections per course (including zero for courses with no sections).
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM course_section_counts v LEFT JOIN (SELECT course_id, COUNT(section_id) AS real_count FROM Sections GROUP BY course_id) s ON v.course_id = s.course_id WHERE (s.real_count IS NULL AND v.section_count<>0) OR (s.real_count IS NOT NULL AND v.section_count<>s.real_count)

tests.purpose: Keys course_id and course_name are not NULL in the view.
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM course_section_counts WHERE course_id IS NULL OR course_name IS NULL

negative_subgoals:
Task: Return the name and id for every course that has fewer than 2 sections associated with it.
Required outputs: course id; course name
Filters: include only courses whose count of associated sections is less than 2 (i.e., 0 or 1 sections); use the course's own id and name values as provided in the schema

views.name: semester_registration_counts
views.body_sql: SELECT s.semester_id, s.semester_name, COUNT(DISTINCT se.student_id) AS registration_count FROM Semesters s JOIN Student_Enrolment se ON se.semester_id = s.semester_id GROUP BY s.semester_id, s.semester_name
views.description: Per-semester count of distinct students registered (aggregated from student enrollment records), including semester id and name for joining.

provenance.question: What is the semester which most student registered in? Show both the name and the id.
provenance.rewrite:
Task: Find the semester during which the largest number of students registered, and return that semester's name and id.
Required outputs: semester name; semester id
Filters: Count registrations per semester across all students; include only semesters that have at least one student registration.
Sort/limit: order by registration count descending and limit to the top 1 (if there are ties, return the semester(s) with the highest count)

tests.purpose: No duplicate rows at the declared grain (semester_id, semester_name)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT semester_id, semester_name, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM semester_registration_counts GROUP BY semester_id, semester_name HAVING cnt > 1)

tests.purpose: registration_count equals COUNT(DISTINCT student_id) computed from base tables for each semester row
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM semester_registration_counts v LEFT JOIN Semesters s ON v.semester_id = s.semester_id LEFT JOIN (SELECT semester_id, COUNT(DISTINCT student_id) AS expected_count FROM Student_Enrolment GROUP BY semester_id) b ON v.semester_id = b.semester_id WHERE (v.registration_count IS NOT b.expected_count) OR (v.registration_count IS NULL AND b.expected_count IS NOT NULL) OR (v.registration_count IS NOT NULL AND b.expected_count IS NULL)

tests.purpose: Keys are not NULL: semester_id and semester_name must be non-NULL
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM semester_registration_counts WHERE semester_id IS NULL OR semester_name IS NULL

views.name: semester_entity_registered_counts
views.body_sql: SELECT s.semester_id AS semester, c.course_id AS id, c.course_name AS name, COUNT(DISTINCT se.student_id) AS registered_students_count FROM Semesters s JOIN Student_Enrolment se ON se.semester_id = s.semester_id JOIN Student_Enrolment_Courses sec ON sec.student_enrolment_id = se.student_enrolment_id JOIN Courses c ON c.course_id = sec.course_id GROUP BY s.semester_id, c.course_id, c.course_name
views.description: Per semester and per entity (course), the count of distinct students registered for that entity in that semester, suitable for finding top entities per semester

provenance.question: For each semester, what is the name and id of the one with the most students registered?
provenance.rewrite:
Task: For each semester, find the single semester-level record corresponding to the course/section/entry that has the largest number of students registered during that semester and return that record's name and id.
Required outputs: semester (the semester identifier used to group records); name (the name of the entity with the most students registered in that semester); id (the id of the entity with the most students registered in that semester); registered_students_count (the number of students registered for that name/id in that semester)
Filters: Group rows by semester. Within each semester, consider only rows that have a non-null registered students count. For each semester return exactly one row: the row whose registered_students_count is maximal for that semester. If there are ties for maximal registered_students_count within a semester, return one of the tied rows (no additional tie-breaker required). Exclude semesters that have no rows with a non-null registered_students_count.
Sort/limit: order by semester ascending; no global row limit (one result row per semester)

tests.purpose: No duplicate rows at the declared grain (semester, id, name)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT semester, id, name, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM semester_entity_registered_counts GROUP BY semester, id, name HAVING cnt > 1) AS t

tests.purpose: registered_students_count matches COUNT(DISTINCT student_id) recomputed from base tables for the same semester+course
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM semester_entity_registered_counts v LEFT JOIN (SELECT s.semester_id AS semester, c.course_id AS id, COUNT(DISTINCT se.student_id) AS expected_count FROM Semesters s JOIN Student_Enrolment se ON se.semester_id = s.semester_id JOIN Student_Enrolment_Courses sec ON sec.student_enrolment_id = se.student_enrolment_id JOIN Courses c ON c.course_id = sec.course_id GROUP BY s.semester_id, c.course_id) b ON v.semester = b.semester AND v.id = b.id WHERE (v.registered_students_count IS NOT b.expected_count) OR (v.registered_students_count IS NULL AND b.expected_count IS NOT NULL) OR (v.registered_students_count IS NOT NULL AND b.expected_count IS NULL)

tests.purpose: Keys (semester, id, name) are not NULL
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM semester_entity_registered_counts WHERE semester IS NULL OR id IS NULL OR name IS NULL

views.name: student_semester_degree_program_counts
views.body_sql: SELECT se.student_id, se.semester_id, COUNT(DISTINCT se.degree_program_id) AS distinct_degree_programs FROM Student_Enrolment se GROUP BY se.student_id, se.semester_id
views.description: For each student and semester, the count of distinct degree programs the student is enrolled in (one row per student per semester).
counter_examples: What are the first, middle, and last names, along with the ids, of all students who enrolled in 2 degree programs in one semester?

provenance.question: Who are enrolled in 2 degree programs in one semester? List the first name, middle name and last name and the id.
provenance.rewrite:
Task: Find all students who are enrolled in exactly two degree programs during a single semester, returning their names and identifier.
Required outputs: first name; middle name; last name; id
Filters: Consider enrollments grouped by student id and semester; include only students whose count of distinct degree programs in the same semester = 2; Semester is identified by the semester field/value present in the enrollment/registration records (use the semester value as-is from the schema); If a student has multiple semesters with two programs, include the student once for the relevant semester rows (one row per student per semester) unless schema/requirements aggregate across semesters; Exclude students with fewer or more than two distinct degree programs in that semester

tests.purpose: No duplicate rows at the declared grain (student_id, semester_id) in the view
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM student_semester_degree_program_counts v JOIN (SELECT student_id, semester_id, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM student_semester_degree_program_counts GROUP BY student_id, semester_id HAVING cnt > 1) dup ON v.student_id = dup.student_id AND v.semester_id = dup.semester_id

tests.purpose: distinct_degree_programs equals count of distinct degree_program_id in base table for that student and semester
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM student_semester_degree_program_counts v LEFT JOIN (SELECT student_id, semester_id, COUNT(DISTINCT degree_program_id) AS expected FROM Student_Enrolment GROUP BY student_id, semester_id) b ON v.student_id = b.student_id AND v.semester_id = b.semester_id WHERE (v.distinct_degree_programs IS NULL AND b.expected IS NOT NULL) OR (v.distinct_degree_programs IS NOT NULL AND b.expected IS NULL) OR (v.distinct_degree_programs IS NOT NULL AND b.expected IS NOT NULL AND v.distinct_degree_programs <> b.expected)

tests.purpose: Every row in the view has non-NULL keys student_id and semester_id and corresponds to an existing student and semester in base tables
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM student_semester_degree_program_counts v WHERE v.student_id IS NULL OR v.semester_id IS NULL OR NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Students s WHERE s.student_id = v.student_id) OR NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Semesters sem WHERE sem.semester_id = v.semester_id)

negative_subgoals:
Task: Find every student who enrolled in exactly two degree programs during the same single semester, and report each such student's first name, middle name, last name, and student id.
Required outputs: first name; middle name; last name; student id
Filters: Include only students who have enrollment records showing they were enrolled in two degree programs where both enrollments have the same semester identifier (i.e., same semester) and those two enrollments occur in the same semester; Count only enrollments that represent distinct degree programs for the same student in that semester; exclude cases where the two records are the same degree program duplicated; Exclude students who enrolled in fewer than 2 or more than 2 degree programs in any single semester; include students for whom there exists at least one semester with exactly 2 distinct degree-program enrollments

views.name: program_kind_enrollment_counts
views.body_sql: SELECT dp.degree_summary_name AS program_kind, COUNT(*) AS student_count FROM Degree_Programs dp JOIN Student_Enrolment se ON se.degree_program_id = dp.degree_program_id GROUP BY dp.degree_summary_name
views.description: Counts of student enrollments per program kind (degree_summary_name), joining degree programs to student enrollments so each enrollment is counted toward its program's kind.

provenance.question: Find the kind of program which most number of students are enrolled in?
provenance.rewrite:
Task: Return the program kind (type of program) that has the largest number of enrolled students — i.e., compute the kind of program for which the count of students enrolled in programs of that kind is maximal.
Required outputs: program kind (the kind/category/name of program); student_count (the number of students enrolled in programs of that kind)
Filters: Consider all students and all program enrollments present in the database (no additional temporal or status filter). Count each student enrollment toward the program kind associated with that student's program. If a student is enrolled in multiple programs, each enrollment counts separately toward the respective program kinds.
Sort/limit: order by student_count desc limit 1

tests.purpose: No NULL program_kind keys: every row's program_kind (key) must be NOT NULL
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM program_kind_enrollment_counts WHERE program_kind IS NULL

tests.purpose: student_count equals number of enrollments in base tables for that program_kind (measure reconciliation)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM program_kind_enrollment_counts v LEFT JOIN (SELECT dp.degree_summary_name AS program_kind, COUNT(*) AS expected_count FROM Degree_Programs dp JOIN Student_Enrolment se ON se.degree_program_id = dp.degree_program_id GROUP BY dp.degree_summary_name) b ON v.program_kind = b.program_kind WHERE b.program_kind IS NULL OR v.student_count != b.expected_count

tests.purpose: No duplicate program_kind rows in the view (grain uniqueness)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) - COUNT(DISTINCT program_kind) FROM program_kind_enrollment_counts

views.name: enrolment_count_per_degree_summary
views.body_sql: SELECT dp.degree_summary_name, COUNT(*) AS enrolment_count FROM Student_Enrolment se JOIN Degree_Programs dp USING(degree_program_id) GROUP BY dp.degree_summary_name
views.description: Counts of enrollment records per degree_summary_name (one row per degree_summary_name with its enrollment record count), useful for summaries and rankings of program popularity.

provenance.question: What is the degree summary name that has the most number of students enrolled?
provenance.rewrite:
Task: Find the degree summary name that has the largest number of students enrolled.
Required outputs: degree summary name; number of students enrolled (the count for that degree summary name)
Filters: Consider all rows in the enrollment data (no additional filtering unless specified elsewhere); Count students per degree summary name; if the same student appears multiple times for the same degree summary name, include each row as an enrollment record unless de-duplication is specified elsewhere
Sort/limit: order by the count of students enrolled in descending order and return the top 1 result

tests.purpose: No duplicate rows per grain: there should be at most one row per degree_summary_name in the view
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT degree_summary_name, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM enrolment_count_per_degree_summary GROUP BY degree_summary_name HAVING cnt > 1)

tests.purpose: Enrolment counts reconcile: enrolment_count must equal the number of Student_Enrolment rows that join to that degree_summary_name
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT v.degree_summary_name FROM enrolment_count_per_degree_summary v LEFT JOIN (SELECT dp.degree_summary_name AS ds, COUNT(*) AS expected_count FROM Student_Enrolment se JOIN Degree_Programs dp USING(degree_program_id) GROUP BY dp.degree_summary_name) b ON v.degree_summary_name = b.ds WHERE (b.expected_count IS NULL AND v.enrolment_count <> 0) OR (b.expected_count IS NOT NULL AND v.enrolment_count != b.expected_count))

tests.purpose: Keys not NULL: every row in the view must have a non-NULL degree_summary_name
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM enrolment_count_per_degree_summary WHERE degree_summary_name IS NULL

views.name: student_enrollment_counts
views.body_sql:
SELECT se.student_id, COUNT(*) AS number_of_enrollments
FROM Student_Enrolment se
GROUP BY se.student_id
views.description: Per-student total count of enrollment records (one row per student with their student_id and enrollment count), useful for ranking or filtering students by how many enrollments they have.

provenance.question: Which student has enrolled for the most times in any program? List the id, first name, middle name, last name, the number of enrollments and student id.
provenance.rewrite:
Task: Find the student(s) who have the highest number of enrollments in any program and return their identifying information along with that enrollment count.
Required outputs: id (the student's unique id); first_name; middle_name; last_name; number_of_enrollments (the count of enrollments for that student across all programs); student_id (duplicate of the student's unique id if 'student id' refers to same field; include if schema has separate 'student id' field)
Filters: Consider all students in the database; include only students whose total count of enrollments (across all programs) equals the maximum such count among all students; Count all enrollment records per student (no date or status filters unless specified elsewhere); Include students even if middle_name is NULL; return NULL or empty as appropriate
Sort/limit: Order results by number_of_enrollments DESC; return all students tied for the maximum count (no numeric limit)

tests.purpose: No duplicate student_id rows in the view (ensures grain is one row per student_id).
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT student_id, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM student_enrollment_counts GROUP BY student_id HAVING cnt > 1)

tests.purpose: number_of_enrollments matches count of Student_Enrolment rows per student_id (measure reconciliation).
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM student_enrollment_counts sec LEFT JOIN (SELECT student_id, COUNT(*) AS expected_count FROM Student_Enrolment GROUP BY student_id) base USING(student_id) WHERE base.expected_count IS NULL OR sec.number_of_enrollments != base.expected_count

tests.purpose: student_id in the view is never NULL (key not NULL).
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM student_enrollment_counts WHERE student_id IS NULL

views.name: student_enrollment_counts_11
views.body_sql: SELECT se.student_id, COUNT(*) AS enrollment_count FROM Student_Enrolment se GROUP BY se.student_id
views.description: Per-student counts of enrollments across all programs (one row per student with their id and enrollment_count).

provenance.question: What is the first, middle, and last name, along with the id and number of enrollments, for the student who enrolled the most in any program?
provenance.rewrite:
Task: Find the student who has the maximum number of enrollments in any program and return that student's first name, middle name, last name, id, and the number of enrollments they have.
Required outputs: first name; middle name; last name; id; number of enrollments
Filters: Consider each student and count how many enrollments they have across all programs; Select the student(s) whose enrollment count equals the maximum enrollment count among all students
Sort/limit: order by number of enrollments descending, limit 1

tests.purpose: No duplicate student_id rows (view should be keyed by student_id)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT student_id, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM student_enrollment_counts_11 GROUP BY student_id HAVING cnt > 1)

tests.purpose: Every enrollment_count equals count of Student_Enrolment rows for that student
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM student_enrollment_counts_11 v LEFT JOIN (SELECT student_id, COUNT(*) AS expected_count FROM Student_Enrolment GROUP BY student_id) b ON v.student_id = b.student_id WHERE (b.expected_count IS NULL AND v.enrollment_count IS NOT NULL) OR (b.expected_count IS NOT NULL AND v.enrollment_count != b.expected_count)

tests.purpose: student_id key is never NULL
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM student_enrollment_counts_11 WHERE student_id IS NULL

views.name: semesters_with_enrollment_counts
views.body_sql: SELECT s.semester_id, s.semester_name, COUNT(e.student_enrolment_id) AS enrollment_count FROM Semesters s LEFT JOIN Student_Enrolment e ON e.semester_id = s.semester_id GROUP BY s.semester_id, s.semester_name
views.description: Per-semester counts of enrollment records (one row per semester with its id, name, and the number of enrollments referencing that semester).

provenance.question: Which semesters do not have any student enrolled? List the semester name.
provenance.rewrite:
Task: Find all semesters (by semester name) for which there are no students enrolled in any course during that semester.
Required outputs: semester name
Filters: Include only semesters where the count of enrolled students is zero across all enrollments referencing that semester. Exclude semesters that have at least one enrollment record linking any student to any course in that semester.

tests.purpose: View has one row per semester (no missing semesters): every semester from Semesters must appear at least once in the view
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Semesters s WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM semesters_with_enrollment_counts v WHERE v.semester_id = s.semester_id AND v.semester_name = s.semester_name)

tests.purpose: View has correct enrollment_count: count matches number of Student_Enrolment rows referencing that semester
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM semesters_with_enrollment_counts v WHERE v.enrollment_count != (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Student_Enrolment e WHERE e.semester_id = v.semester_id)

tests.purpose: View grain uniqueness: no duplicate rows for the declared key (semester_id, semester_name)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT semester_id, semester_name, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM semesters_with_enrollment_counts GROUP BY semester_id, semester_name HAVING cnt > 1) t

views.name: courses_with_enrollments
views.body_sql: SELECT DISTINCT c.course_id, c.course_name FROM Courses c JOIN Student_Enrolment_Courses sec ON sec.course_id = c.course_id
views.description: All courses that have at least one student enrollment (course identifiers and names) to be reused for queries needing courses that are actually taken by students.

provenance.question: What are all the course names of the courses which ever have students enrolled in?
provenance.rewrite:
Task: Return the names of all distinct courses that have had at least one student enrolled at any time.
Required outputs: course_name
Filters: Include only courses for which there exists at least one enrollment record linking a student to that course (i.e., courses with one or more enrollments). Exclude courses with zero enrollments.

tests.purpose: View rows match the declared grain: no duplicate (course_id, course_name) pairs
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT course_id, course_name, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM courses_with_enrollments GROUP BY course_id, course_name HAVING cnt > 1)

tests.purpose: Every row in the view corresponds to an existing course in Courses (no dangling course_id)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM courses_with_enrollments v LEFT JOIN Courses c ON v.course_id = c.course_id WHERE c.course_id IS NULL

tests.purpose: Every row in the view has at least one matching enrollment in Student_Enrolment_Courses
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM courses_with_enrollments v LEFT JOIN Student_Enrolment_Courses sec ON v.course_id = sec.course_id WHERE sec.student_course_id IS NULL

views.name: courses_with_enrollments_14
views.body_sql:
SELECT c.course_id, c.course_name
FROM Courses c
JOIN Student_Enrolment_Courses sec ON sec.course_id = c.course_id
JOIN Student_Enrolment se ON se.student_enrolment_id = sec.student_enrolment_id
GROUP BY c.course_id, c.course_name
views.description: List of courses that have one or more student enrollments (one row per course with its id and name), suitable as a reusable cohort of courses that currently have enrolled students.

provenance.question: What are the names of all courses that have some students enrolled?
provenance.rewrite:
Task: Return the names of every course that currently has one or more students enrolled in it.
Required outputs: course name (one row per course name)
Filters: include only courses for which there exists at least one enrollment/registration linking a student to that course (i.e. courses with enrollment count > 0)

tests.purpose: View has one row per course (no duplicate course_id/course_name pairs)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT course_id, course_name, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM courses_with_enrollments_14 GROUP BY course_id, course_name HAVING cnt > 1)

tests.purpose: Every row in the view corresponds to an existing course (course_id exists in Courses)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM courses_with_enrollments_14 v WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Courses c WHERE c.course_id = v.course_id)

tests.purpose: Every course in the view has at least one current enrollment (recompute from base tables and find mismatches)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM courses_with_enrollments_14 v WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Student_Enrolment_Courses sec JOIN Student_Enrolment se ON sec.student_enrolment_id = se.student_enrolment_id WHERE sec.course_id = v.course_id)

views.name: course_enrollment_counts
views.body_sql:
SELECT course_id, COUNT(*) AS enrol_count
FROM Student_Enrolment_Courses
GROUP BY course_id
views.description: Per-course enrollment counts counted from the Student_Enrolment_Courses table to provide total enrollments per course (one row per course_id).

provenance.question: What's the name of the course with most number of enrollments?
provenance.rewrite:
Task: Find the name of the course that has the largest number of enrollments (i.e., the course with the highest enrollment count).
Required outputs: course name
Filters: Consider all courses and all enrollments in the database; count enrollments per course and identify the course(s) with the maximum count.
Sort/limit: order by enrollment count descending, limit 1 (if multiple courses tie for max, return the name for any one or return all tied names depending on downstream handling)

tests.purpose: View has one row per course_id (no duplicate course_id values)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM course_enrollment_counts c JOIN (SELECT course_id, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM course_enrollment_counts GROUP BY course_id HAVING cnt > 1) d ON c.course_id = d.course_id

tests.purpose: course_id (the key) is never NULL in the view
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM course_enrollment_counts WHERE course_id IS NULL

views.name: course_enrollment_counts_16

views.description: Per-course enrollment counts based on the student_enrolment_courses table (one row per course with the number of student enrollments)

provenance.question: What is the name of the course with the most students enrolled?
provenance.rewrite:
Task: Find the name of the course that has the highest number of students enrolled.
Required outputs: course name (single value)

tests.purpose: No duplicate course_id rows in the view (ensures view grain is one row per course_id)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM course_enrollment_counts_16 v GROUP BY v.course_id HAVING COUNT(*)>1 LIMIT 1

tests.purpose: enrollment_count matches COUNT(*) of Student_Enrolment_Courses per course_id
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM course_enrollment_counts_16 v LEFT JOIN (SELECT course_id, COUNT(*) AS expected_count FROM Student_Enrolment_Courses GROUP BY course_id) s ON v.course_id = s.course_id WHERE (s.expected_count IS NULL AND v.enrollment_count IS NOT NULL) OR (s.expected_count IS NOT NULL AND v.enrollment_count != s.expected_count)

tests.purpose: course_id in the view is never NULL (key not null)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM course_enrollment_counts_16 WHERE course_id IS NULL

views.name: transcript_course_result_counts
views.body_sql: SELECT t.transcript_id, t.transcript_date, COUNT(tc.student_course_id) AS course_result_count FROM Transcripts t JOIN Transcript_Contents tc ON tc.transcript_id = t.transcript_id GROUP BY t.transcript_id, t.transcript_date
views.description: Per-transcript counts of associated course result rows (one row per transcript with transcript_id and transcript_date and the count of related student_course_id), useful for filtering transcripts by how many course results they contain
validated_on: What is the date and id of the transcript with at least 2 courses listed?

provenance.question: Show the date and id of the transcript with at least 2 course results.

tests.purpose: No duplicate rows at the declared grain (transcript_id, transcript_date)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT transcript_id, transcript_date, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM transcript_course_result_counts GROUP BY transcript_id, transcript_date HAVING cnt > 1)

tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM transcript_course_result_counts v LEFT JOIN Transcripts t ON v.transcript_id = t.transcript_id WHERE (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Transcript_Contents tc WHERE tc.transcript_id = v.transcript_id) IS NULL AND v.course_result_count IS NOT NULL OR (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Transcript_Contents tc WHERE tc.transcript_id = v.transcript_id) != v.course_result_count

positive_subgoals:
Task: Return the date and id of each transcript that lists at least 2 courses.

views.name: students_min_registration_time
views.body_sql: SELECT student_id, first_name, middle_name, last_name, date_first_registered FROM Students WHERE date_first_registered IS NOT NULL AND date_first_registered = (SELECT MIN(date_first_registered) FROM Students WHERE date_first_registered IS NOT NULL)
views.description: For each student, their registration timestamp; includes only students with a non-null registration timestamp and identifies those with the minimum registration timestamp across all students.
validated_on: What is the first, middle, and last name of the first student to register?

provenance.question: Who is the first student to register? List the first name, middle name and last name.
provenance.rewrite:
Task: Return the student (first name, middle name, last name) who registered earliest (i.e., has the earliest registration timestamp) — if multiple students share the exact earliest registration time, return all of them.
Required outputs: first name; middle name; last name
Filters: consider only rows representing students with a non-null registration timestamp; treat 'first to register' as the minimum value of the registration timestamp/time field
Sort/limit: order by registration timestamp ascending; limit 1 (or return all rows tied for the minimum timestamp)

tests.purpose: View has exactly one row per student_id (no duplicate student_id in the view)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT student_id, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM students_min_registration_time GROUP BY student_id HAVING cnt <> 1)

tests.purpose: Every row in the view has a non-NULL date_first_registered
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM students_min_registration_time WHERE date_first_registered IS NULL

tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM students_min_registration_time v WHERE v.date_first_registered <> (SELECT MIN(date_first_registered) FROM Students WHERE date_first_registered IS NOT NULL) OR (SELECT MIN(date_first_registered) FROM Students WHERE date_first_registered IS NOT NULL) IS NULL

positive_subgoals:
Task: Find the first student who registered and return that student's first name, middle name, and last name.
Required outputs: first name; middle name; last name
Filters: the row must be the student with the earliest registration time (i.e., minimal registration timestamp/date); if multiple students share the identical earliest registration time, return the one that is first according to any deterministic tie-breaker (e.g., lowest student id)

views.name: students_with_graduation_date
views.body_sql: SELECT student_id, first_name, middle_name, last_name, date_left AS graduation_date FROM Students WHERE date_left IS NOT NULL
views.description: All student records that include a graduation date (date_left) with student identifiers and name fields for use in cohort or earliest-graduate calculations.

provenance.question: What is the first, middle, and last name of the earliest school graduate?
provenance.rewrite:
Task: Find the first name, middle name, and last name of the person who is the earliest school graduate (i.e., the graduate with the earliest graduation date).
Required outputs: first name; middle name; last name
Filters: Consider only records representing school graduates.; If graduation date is stored, use that date to determine earliest (minimum) graduation date across all graduates.; If multiple graduates share the same earliest graduation date, return all such graduates.
Sort/limit: order by graduation date ascending; no limit (return all ties for earliest date)

tests.purpose: View grain: no duplicate student_id (each student_id appears at most once)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT student_id, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM students_with_graduation_date GROUP BY student_id HAVING cnt > 1) AS t

tests.purpose: Every row in the view corresponds to a Students row with a non-NULL date_left and matching name fields
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM students_with_graduation_date v LEFT JOIN Students s USING(student_id) WHERE s.student_id IS NULL OR s.date_left IS NULL OR v.graduation_date != s.date_left OR v.first_name IS NULL OR v.last_name IS NULL

tests.purpose: View does not include any Students rows that have NULL date_left (completeness w.r.t. filter)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Students s WHERE s.date_left IS NOT NULL AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM students_with_graduation_date v WHERE v.student_id = s.student_id AND v.graduation_date = s.date_left)

views.name: students_with_different_permanent_and_current_address
views.body_sql: SELECT student_id, first_name, last_name, permanent_address_id, current_address_id FROM Students WHERE permanent_address_id IS NOT NULL AND current_address_id IS NOT NULL AND permanent_address_id <> current_address_id
views.description: List of students where the permanent address_id differs from the current address_id (returns student identifiers and basic name fields and both address ids) — useful as a cohort of students whose stored permanent and current addresses are not the same.

provenance.question: What is the first name of the student whose permanent address is different from his or her current one?
provenance.rewrite:
Task: Return the first name(s) of student(s) whose permanent address is different from their current address.
Required outputs: first name of student
Filters: rows where the student's permanent address != student's current address (compare the two address fields for inequality)

tests.purpose: View rows follow the view filter: both address ids are non-NULL and different
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM students_with_different_permanent_and_current_address v LEFT JOIN Students s USING(student_id) WHERE NOT (v.permanent_address_id IS NOT NULL AND v.current_address_id IS NOT NULL AND v.permanent_address_id <> v.current_address_id)

tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Students s WHERE s.permanent_address_id IS NOT NULL AND s.current_address_id IS NOT NULL AND s.permanent_address_id <> s.current_address_id AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM students_with_different_permanent_and_current_address v WHERE v.student_id = s.student_id)

tests.purpose: View grain uniqueness: student_id is unique in the view (no duplicates)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT student_id, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM students_with_different_permanent_and_current_address GROUP BY student_id HAVING cnt > 1)

views.name: students_per_current_address
views.body_sql: SELECT s.current_address_id AS address_id, COUNT(DISTINCT s.student_id) AS student_count FROM Students s WHERE s.current_address_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY s.current_address_id
views.description: Per-address counts of distinct students currently associated with each address (joins Students to Addresses via the student's current_address_id).
counter_examples: What are the different addresses that have students living there?

provenance.question: Which address holds the most number of students currently? List the address id and all lines.
provenance.rewrite:
Task: Find the address (address id and all address lines) that currently has the largest number of students residing at it.
Required outputs: address id; all address lines (every column in the schema that represents parts of the address, e.g., line1, line2, city, state, postal_code, etc.); the count of students currently at that address (optional but may be included to determine the maximum)
Filters: Only consider students who are currently associated with an address (i.e., exclude NULL or missing address references).; If the schema distinguishes current vs historical student-address associations, include only associations marked as current (e.g., a boolean/current_flag or by using an association table with effective date ranges where current means the range includes today).; If a student can be associated with multiple addresses simultaneously, count each student once per address they are currently associated with (i.e., count student-address associations that meet the "current" criterion).
Sort/limit: Order by student count descending and limit to the top 1 result; if there are ties and multiple addresses share the maximum count, return all such addresses (no additional limit).

tests.purpose: No duplicate address_id rows in the view (grain uniqueness)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT address_id, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM students_per_current_address GROUP BY address_id HAVING cnt > 1)

tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM students_per_current_address v LEFT JOIN (SELECT current_address_id AS address_id, COUNT(DISTINCT student_id) AS expected_count FROM Students WHERE current_address_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY current_address_id) b ON v.address_id = b.address_id WHERE b.address_id IS NULL OR v.student_count != b.expected_count

tests.purpose: address_id (key) is never NULL in the view
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM students_per_current_address WHERE address_id IS NULL

negative_subgoals:
Task: List the distinct addresses that have one or more students living at them.

views.name: address_student_counts

views.description: Per-address counts of distinct students who reference that address as current or permanent (one row per address_id with its lines and student count)

provenance.question: What is the id, line 1, and line 2 of the address with the most students?
provenance.rewrite:

tests.purpose: Every row's address_id is non-NULL and exists in Addresses (key not NULL and join did not drop/duplicate addresses present in Addresses with any referencing student)

views.name: transcript_printed_timestamps
views.body_sql: SELECT transcript_id, transcript_date AS printed_timestamp FROM Transcripts WHERE transcript_date IS NOT NULL
views.description: All transcript records with their printed datetime/timestamp for use in general time-based calculations or joins

provenance.question: On average, when were the transcripts printed?
provenance.rewrite:
Task: Compute the average (mean) of the dates/times when transcripts were printed.
Required outputs: average printed date/time of transcripts (single scalar value representing the mean of the 'printed' timestamp for all transcript records)
Filters: include all transcript records with a non-null printed date/time; exclude records where printed is null

tests.purpose: No duplicate transcript_id in the view (ensures grain is respected)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT transcript_id FROM transcript_printed_timestamps GROUP BY transcript_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 1)

tests.purpose: Every row in the view corresponds to a base Transcripts row with same non-NULL transcript_date (ensures view doesn't introduce rows or change timestamps)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM transcript_printed_timestamps v LEFT JOIN Transcripts t ON v.transcript_id = t.transcript_id WHERE t.transcript_id IS NULL OR v.printed_timestamp IS NULL OR v.printed_timestamp != t.transcript_date

tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Transcripts t WHERE t.transcript_date IS NOT NULL AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM transcript_printed_timestamps v WHERE v.transcript_id = t.transcript_id AND v.printed_timestamp = t.transcript_date)

views.name: transcripts_with_valid_transcript_date
views.body_sql: SELECT transcript_id, transcript_date FROM Transcripts WHERE transcript_date IS NOT NULL
views.description: All transcripts that have a non-NULL, valid transcript_date value (keeps id and date for reuse in aggregates or joins).

provenance.question: What is the average transcript date?
provenance.rewrite:
Task: Compute the average (mean) of the transcript date values across all rows in the dataset
Required outputs: average_transcript_date: a single value representing the mean of the transcript date values (expressed in the same date/time resolution as the transcript date column, e.g., date or timestamp)

tests.purpose: No duplicate transcript_id in the view (view should be keyed by transcript_id).
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT transcript_id, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM transcripts_with_valid_transcript_date GROUP BY transcript_id HAVING cnt > 1) AS t

tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM transcripts_with_valid_transcript_date v LEFT JOIN Transcripts t USING (transcript_id) WHERE t.transcript_id IS NULL OR (t.transcript_date IS NULL) OR (t.transcript_date != v.transcript_date)

views.name: enrollment_transcript_counts
views.body_sql: SELECT sec.student_course_id AS enrollment_id, COUNT(DISTINCT tc.transcript_id) AS transcript_count FROM Student_Enrolment_Courses AS sec LEFT JOIN Transcript_Contents AS tc ON sec.student_course_id = tc.student_course_id GROUP BY sec.student_course_id
views.description: Per-enrollment (student_course_id) count of distinct transcripts in which that enrollment appears (one row per enrollment with its transcript occurrence count).

provenance.question: What is the maximum number of times that a course shows up in different transcripts and what is that course's enrollment id?
provenance.rewrite:
Task: Find the course that appears the maximum number of times across different transcripts and report that maximum count along with that course's enrollment id.
Required outputs: enrollment id of the course (enrollment id); maximum number of times that course appears in different transcripts (count)
Filters: Consider all transcript records available; count distinct transcript occurrences per enrollment id.; If multiple enrollment ids tie for the maximum count, include the enrollment id(s) that achieve that maximum.

tests.purpose: Every enrollment in the view corresponds to an existing Student_Enrolment_Courses row (no phantom enrollments)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM enrollment_transcript_counts v LEFT JOIN Student_Enrolment_Courses sec ON v.enrollment_id = sec.student_course_id WHERE sec.student_course_id IS NULL

tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM enrollment_transcript_counts WHERE enrollment_id IS NULL

tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM enrollment_transcript_counts v JOIN Student_Enrolment_Courses sec ON v.enrollment_id = sec.student_course_id LEFT JOIN (SELECT student_course_id, COUNT(DISTINCT transcript_id) AS expected_count FROM Transcript_Contents GROUP BY student_course_id) tc ON v.enrollment_id = tc.student_course_id WHERE COALESCE(v.transcript_count,0) != COALESCE(tc.expected_count,0)

views.name: transcript_result_counts
views.body_sql: SELECT t.transcript_id, t.transcript_date, COUNT(tc.student_course_id) AS number_of_results FROM Transcripts t LEFT JOIN Transcript_Contents tc ON t.transcript_id = tc.transcript_id GROUP BY t.transcript_id, t.transcript_date
views.description: Per-transcript count of associated transcript_content rows (number of results) for each transcript_id and its date.

provenance.question: Show the date of the transcript which shows the least number of results, also list the id.
provenance.rewrite:
Task: Find the transcript date (the date of the transcript) and the transcript id for the transcript row that has the smallest number of results (i.e., the minimum value in the 'number of results' field) across all transcripts.
Required outputs: transcript date (the date value identifying when the transcript occurred); transcript id (the identifier of that transcript)
Filters: consider all transcript rows; identify the row(s) whose 'number of results' value is equal to the global minimum 'number of results' across all transcripts; if multiple transcripts tie for the minimum 'number of results', include all tied rows
Sort/limit: no specific ordering required; return all rows that meet the minimum criterion (no limit), or optionally order by transcript id ascending

tests.purpose: No duplicate rows at the declared grain (transcript_id, transcript_date)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT transcript_id, transcript_date, COUNT(*) AS c FROM transcript_result_counts GROUP BY transcript_id, transcript_date HAVING c > 1)

tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM transcript_result_counts v LEFT JOIN (SELECT transcript_id, COUNT(*) AS expected_count FROM Transcript_Contents GROUP BY transcript_id) b ON v.transcript_id = b.transcript_id WHERE (b.expected_count IS NULL AND v.number_of_results != 0) OR (b.expected_count IS NOT NULL AND v.number_of_results != b.expected_count)

tests.purpose: Keys not NULL: transcript_id and transcript_date must be present for every row
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM transcript_result_counts WHERE transcript_id IS NULL OR transcript_date IS NULL

views.name: transcript_results_count
views.body_sql:
SELECT t.transcript_id, t.transcript_date, COUNT(tc.student_course_id) AS results_count
FROM Transcripts t
LEFT JOIN Transcript_Contents tc ON tc.transcript_id = t.transcript_id
GROUP BY t.transcript_id, t.transcript_date
views.description: Per-transcript row with its id, date, and count of associated transcript_content rows (a measure of results) for use in filtering or ranking transcripts.

provenance.question: What is the date and id of the transcript with the least number of results?
provenance.rewrite:
Task: Find the transcript row that has the smallest value in its 'results' column, and return that transcript's date and id.
Required outputs: date; id
Filters: Select rows from the transcripts table where results is equal to the minimum results value across all transcripts (i.e., results = (SELECT MIN(results) FROM transcripts))
Sort/limit: If multiple transcripts tie for the minimum results, return all tied rows (no additional ordering or limit).

tests.purpose: No duplicate rows at the declared grain (transcript_id, transcript_date)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT transcript_id, transcript_date, COUNT(*) as cnt FROM transcript_results_count GROUP BY transcript_id, transcript_date HAVING cnt > 1)

tests.purpose: results_count equals count of Transcript_Contents rows per transcript (reconcile measure with base tables)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM transcript_results_count v LEFT JOIN Transcripts t ON v.transcript_id = t.transcript_id AND (v.transcript_date = t.transcript_date) WHERE v.results_count != (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Transcript_Contents tc WHERE tc.transcript_id = v.transcript_id)

tests.purpose: Keys not NULL: transcript_id and transcript_date must be present for every view row
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM transcript_results_count WHERE transcript_id IS NULL OR transcript_date IS NULL

views.name: semester_enrollment_degree_level_counts
views.body_sql:

FROM Student_Enrolment se
JOIN Degree_Programs dp ON se.degree_program_id = dp.degree_program_id
GROUP BY se.semester_id, dp.degree_summary_name
views.description: Per semester and degree_summary_name, counts of enrollments (links semesters to degree program degree levels present in that semester). Useful to find semesters that have enrollments for particular degree levels or to test co-occurrence of degree levels in a semester.

provenance.question: Find the semester when both Master students and Bachelor students got enrolled in.
provenance.rewrite:
Task: Find the semester value(s) for which there exist enrolled students of both 'Master' and 'Bachelor' degree levels.
Required outputs: semester — the semester identifier (as stored in the database) for which both a Master student and a Bachelor student are enrolled
Filters: Consider only rows where a student's degree level equals 'Master' and rows where a student's degree level equals 'Bachelor'. Return semesters that appear in at least one 'Master' enrollment row and at least one 'Bachelor' enrollment row.

tests.purpose: View rows are unique at the declared grain (semester_id, degree_summary_name). Detect duplicate view rows with same key appearing more than once.
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT semester_id, degree_summary_name, COUNT(*) AS ct FROM semester_enrollment_degree_level_counts GROUP BY semester_id, degree_summary_name HAVING ct > 1)

tests.purpose: Every row's enrollment_count matches the count of Student_Enrolment rows joined to Degree_Programs for that semester_id and degree_summary_name.
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM semester_enrollment_degree_level_counts v LEFT JOIN (SELECT se.semester_id, dp.degree_summary_name, COUNT(*) AS expected_count FROM Student_Enrolment se JOIN Degree_Programs dp ON se.degree_program_id = dp.degree_program_id GROUP BY se.semester_id, dp.degree_summary_name) b ON v.semester_id = b.semester_id AND v.degree_summary_name = b.degree_summary_name WHERE (b.expected_count IS NULL AND v.enrollment_count IS NOT NULL) OR (b.expected_count IS NOT NULL AND v.enrollment_count != b.expected_count)

tests.purpose: Keys are not NULL: semester_id and degree_summary_name must be present for every view row.
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM semester_enrollment_degree_level_counts WHERE semester_id IS NULL OR degree_summary_name IS NULL

views.name: enrolments_with_degree_summary_per_semester
views.body_sql:

views.description: Per-semester counts of enrolments broken down by degree summary name (e.g., Bachelor, Master), keeping keys to join by semester and degree program.

provenance.question: What is the id of the semester that had both Masters and Bachelors students enrolled?
provenance.rewrite:
Task: Find the semester id for the semester(s) in which students from both the Masters level and the Bachelors level were enrolled.
Required outputs: semester id (the identifier value of the semester)
Filters: Include only semesters where there exists at least one enrolled student whose level is 'Masters' and at least one enrolled student whose level is 'Bachelors' during that same semester.

tests.purpose: No duplicate rows at the declared grain (semester_id, degree_summary_name). Fails if the view contains two or more rows with same keys.
